s1.quote: The Stanegarth lies in 20m. … At only 18.7m long and 71 tons … There are no obstructions inside.

s2.quote: The Stangarth can be found on a 190° bearing form the Bus Stop (A). The Stangarth can also be found on a 220° bearing form slip way (B).

s4.quote: The wreck now sits in 20 metres (66 ft) of fresh water

s3.quote: Stanegarth is one of Stoney Cove's most popular diving features and the UK's most dived wreck.

penetration.value: Interior cleared of obstructions for swim-throughs

highlights.text: Largest inland wreck in a UK dive centre

summary.text: A 1910 steam tug sunk in a flooded Leicestershire quarry as a training and attraction wreck. It lies in about 20 m, has been stripped so divers can swim through, and is among the most visited wrecks in Britain.

s1.quote: The site has a range of depths to 36 metres (118 ft).

s2.quote: with depths of 7 metres (entry level), 22 metres (intermediate) and 36 metres (expert). … beware the deep silt, which can reduce visibility to zero.

highlights.text: Stanegarth tug, bus, Viscount cockpit, galleon

hazards.text: Deep silt can drop visibility to zero

summary.text: A flooded inland quarry with terraced zones from about 7 m for beginners to 36 m for experts, scattered with sunken vehicles, aircraft parts and the Stanegarth tug. Silt at depth can kill visibility.

s1.quote: there is quite a sudden drop-off to 24m there, so decent buoyancy control is key. … Access is very easy, just kit up and in you go.

s2.quote: The quarry itself reaches a depth of 26 metres. … Visibility was good, around six metres.

highlights.text: Plane, cars and vans on the bottom

hazards.text: Sudden drop-off to 24 m; needs good buoyancy

summary.text: A Staffordshire inland quarry with easy walk-in access, shallow training platforms and a steep drop to roughly 24-26 m. Sunken vehicles, a plane and trees add interest, and pike and sturgeon live there.

s1.quote: The wrecksite is designated as a Protected Place under the Protection of Military Remains Act 1986.

access.value: Protected Place under the Protection of Military Remains Act 1986 (war grave)

s1.quote: Dorothea has a max of 104.5m deep, in the sump tunnel, but most of it bottoms out at around 87 ish … Dive to your experiance this can be a dangerous dive.

s2.quote: the deepest dropping 106m from the surface … under license from the landowner, through the North Wales Technical Divers club … access is strictly limited to those with appropriate qualifications

access.value: Landowner licence via a local technical diving club; qualified divers only

hazards.text: Great depth and cold; dive within experience
Steep entry ramp and potholed access track

summary.text: A flooded Welsh slate quarry with vertical pits reaching over 100 m, most of it bottoming near 87 m. It has a serious safety record, and diving is now only by licence for qualified divers.

s1.quote: good visibility and depths ranging from 6–18 metres (20–59 ft) … a platform at 6 metres (20 ft), plus flooded buildings, boats, a van and a gnome garden

s2.quote: 20m max depth … submarine, rails, and wagons … register and pay an entry fee

s3.quote: Our maximum depth reached was 15 metres.

access.value: Operator-run site; entry fee; check current opening status

highlights.text: Flooded buildings, boats, van and a submarine

summary.text: A flooded slate quarry section at Llanberis with a platform at 6 m and a floor around 18-20 m. Divers pass old mine buildings, rails and sunken boats; entry is through the on-site dive operator.

s1.quote: good visibility and depths ranging from 6–18 metres (20–59 ft)

notDiveSite.reason: Large slate quarry complex; only the flooded Vivian section is dived

s1.quote: can be seen at around 10 metres … some stunning reefs as little as 80-100 metres from the shore

s2.quote: 15m … a very nice reef about 80m out … Speedboats and jet skis

hazards.text: Speedboats and jet skis; use an SMB

summary.text: A sheltered Anglesey bay dived from the beach, with a rocky reef roughly 80-100 m offshore reaching about 15 m at high tide and a few old wrecks around 10 m.

s1.quote: perfect dive location for beginners. With a fairly gradual incline, the beach also makes for easy entrance and exit from the water. … The seabed is mostly sand with some rocky outcrops
not worth repairing … sold … returned to service as a merchant ship

sites.name: HMY Mary

s1.quote: designated as a Historic Wreck under Protections of Wrecks Act 1973 … which extend from 5m to 25m water depth … very exposed to southerly and westerly winds and strong currents

s2.quote: the south-west corner of The Skerries

access.value: Protected wreck (Protection of Wrecks Act 1973); diving needs a Welsh Government licence

summary.text: A royal yacht lost in 1675 at the Skerries off Anglesey, now a heavily concreted ballast mound at the foot of a cliff with finds in rocky gullies. It is a designated historic wreck and exposed to wind and tide.

sites.depthNote: Gullies hold remains from 5 m to 25 m

s1.quote: designated as a controlled site under the Protection of Military Remains Act

notDiveSite.reason: Controlled site under the Protection of Military Remains Act; diving prohibited without MoD licence

s1.quote: these three warship wrecks can no longer be dived without written permission from the MoD

notDiveSite.reason: Designated a Controlled Site; cannot be dived without written MoD permission

sites.name: La Combattante

s1.quote: The forepart of La Combattante lays in 11 meters of water … the afterpart lays in 25 meters of water

sites.depthNote: Forepart in 11 m, afterpart in 25 m

s1.quote: The typical depth is 0-20 Metres 0-60 Feet. … The typical visibility is 3-10 Metres 10-30 Feet.

s2.quote: various depths from 3m to 9m … ropes have been strung between each underwater 'feature' to aid navigation

s3.quote: easy to navigate with the ropes and bearings … The visibility was good

summary.text: A flooded Lancashire stone quarry used for training and fun diving, with platforms between 3 and 9 m, rope trails linking sunken features and a floor around 20 m. Visibility is typically 3-10 m.

s2.quote: Below 100 feet the murky waves is a wreck … In 2008 the forgotten wreck was visited by Polish divers.

summary.text: A large Polish liner that sank off the Humber coast and lies in about 30-34 m. Left undiscovered for decades, it was visited and filmed by Polish divers in 2008.
